title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: US equity futures rose Monday (S&P +0.3%, Nasdaq +0.5%, Dow +0.36%) after the Dow's third straight losing week (-1.7%, worst since March), ahead of Thursday's Trump-Xi summit.
Markets: The 10-year Treasury yield eased to ~4.97% after touching 5.00% Friday; Brent crude slid ~1.8% to ~$102/bbl on Middle East diplomacy hopes.

Markets: Asia mixed-to-higher - Kospi +1.5% on chip strength, Shanghai +0.4%, Hang Seng +0.4% (tech-led); Nikkei closed for a holiday after Friday's +1.4% close at 65,019 following the BOJ's hike to 1.25%.
Companies: Nvidia and OpenAI's $100B, 10-gigawatt infrastructure partnership continues to drive sentiment across AI and chip stocks.
Macro/Policy: The Fed's 25bp hike to 3.75%-4.00% on Sept. 16 (first since 2023) remains the dominant backdrop, with markets now pricing another hike later in 2026.

Macro/Policy: Trump and Xi meet Thursday, Sept. 24 in Washington - trade truce extension, tariffs and AI chips on the agenda; no breakthrough deal is expected (Goldman's base case is a 'delay,' not a deal).
Macro/Policy: Iran-backed Houthis attacked Saudi Arabia with missiles and drones over the weekend, and US-Iran tensions escalated, keeping Middle East risk elevated.
